newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Conservatives get convention bounce.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Conservatives get convention bounce.

text.p: Canada's beleaguered Conservatives got a boost in popularity from their policy convention last month but still badly trail the ruling Liberals, a poll released on Friday showed.
The Angus Reid poll for the Southam News chain showed the Conservatives moving to second place with the support of 17 percent of the population in August from 12 percent in July.

The Conservatives gained a nationwide audience with their convention in Winnipeg in late August, shortly before the Aug. 27-30 poll was taken. They left their right-wing rivals, the Reform Party, behind with an unchanged 12 percent. Reform has 51 seats in Parliament to just two for the Conservatives.
But the Liberals maintained a solid lead with support of 53 percent of those polled. They have polled at 49 percent or more since winning the 1993 election with 41 percent.
The poll has a margin of error of 2.5 percent.
